answer.rationale: Memory c2 is the only record directly addressing the low-cost vendor as a primary supplier: cost-cut performance, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy. The current situation mirrors that scenario — a single vendor quote that meets the mandated 18% reduction on its own, with the incumbent refusing to renegotiate. Verifying c2 confirms whether the prior switch held up operationally or whether hidden costs (quality, lead-time, reconciliation) emerged that would affect total cost of ownership. If the archive corroborates the consolidated summary, switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor is the lowest-TCO path that does not introduce new delivery risk beyond what was already accepted in the earlier cycle. The assembly-line buffer concern is mitigated by the fact that the low-cost vendor is already the quoted alternative and the primary contract lapses in 14 days; deferring or negotiating with a vendor who has already refused to move on price would either miss the deadline or miss the finance mandate. One sourcing decision this cycle: switch_primary_vendor.
